recent_outcomes.hypothesis: The loop should preserve the champion's successful raw-evidence solo reasoning and A-B-A-B admission gate while emitting a smaller, less interaction-prone repair stack. Removing superseded or final-context-harmful edits should reduce accumulated overfitting and improve paired consistency and median strength without increasing invalid engines.

The champion cannot revoke such a stale acceptance certificate based on an exact intervention in the final assembled engine.
recent_outcomes.strengths: Extends executable causal attribution from edit admission to final repair-stack membership.; Preserves the promoted solo organization, raw evidence, exact rollback, and one continuous engine trajectory.; Can eliminate redundant logic, duplicated work, and adverse interactions introduced by individually valid repairs.; Uses counterfactual source ablations rather than replicated model calls, candidate sampling, or best-of-N selection.; Can emit the unchanged champion when no complete valid repair stack survives.
recent_outcomes.weaknesses: A bounded regression suite may classify a repair as redundant even though it provides strength outside the observed obligations.; Final-context ablation and replay consume execution budget and may reduce the number of initial repairs attempted.; Nondeterministic search behavior can make a necessary patch appear dispensable.; Removing an older patch can alter the context in which another retained patch was assessed, requiring bounded invalidation and replay.; Code simplification may improve robustness without producing enough Elo gain to satisfy paired promotion.
